subject: mathematics_2b
question_text: Find the equation of the circle passing through the points (2,1), (5,5), (−6,7).

insider_note: The centre has a fraction in it, so rounding −1/2 to 0 makes every later value wrong — carry the fraction all the way and clear it at the final multiplication.

steps.label: First equation from SA = SB
steps.margin_note: One mark. The numbers are larger here than in the earlier questions, so expand in two clear rows rather than one long line.
steps.memory_tip: Same three steps every time: square, cancel the second-degree terms, tidy.
lines: Let S(x₁, y₁) be the centre of the circle.
steps.why: The squared terms cancel across the equals sign, so what is left is a straight line — the perpendicular bisector of AB. The centre must lie on it.
common_mistakes: Collecting 4 + 1 = 5 on the left and 25 + 25 = 50 on the right, then subtracting the wrong way.
Dividing by 2 and losing the odd constant 45.

steps.label: Second equation from SA = SC
steps.margin_note: Second mark. C has a negative x, so (x₁ + 6)² gives +12x₁ — the sign that is missed most often.
steps.memory_tip: C = (−6, 7) gives brackets (x₁ + 6) and (y₁ − 7). Change the sign of the coordinate.
steps.why: This is the perpendicular bisector of AC. Dividing through by −4 keeps the coefficients small, which matters when the two lines are solved together.
common_mistakes: Dividing −16x₁ + 12y₁ − 80 = 0 by −4 and forgetting to change all three signs.

steps.label: Solve for the centre
steps.margin_note: Two marks. Elimination is written here; the book uses cross-multiplication and reaches the same pair.
steps.memory_tip: Multiply (1) by 3 and (2) by 8 to make the y coefficients 24 and −24, then add.
steps.why: Two straight lines meet at exactly one point, which is the centre. Making the y coefficients equal and opposite removes y in one addition.
common_mistakes: Substituting x₁ = −1/2 into (1) and mishandling the fraction.

steps.label: Find the radius
steps.margin_note: One mark. Keep r² as the improper fraction 125/4 — turning it into a decimal loses accuracy in the last step.
lines: A = (2, 1) lies on the circle, so r = SA.
steps.why: The centre has a fraction, so r² is a fraction too. Writing 25 as 100/4 keeps one common denominator through to the end.

steps.label: Equation of the circle
steps.margin_note: The last two marks. The fractions clear only at the constant: 1/4 + 36 − 125/4 = 5.
lines: Circle with centre (−1/2, 6) and r² = 125/4 is
steps.why: Every constant is written over 4 so they can be combined in one step: 1 + 144 − 125 = 20, and 20/4 = 5. The fractions disappear and the answer is a clean integer equation.
common_mistakes: Forgetting to bring 125/4 across before combining the constants.
